[00:38] That's the headline. But what makes it powerful is how it structures that building process around four core components. Let me walk you through each one. Topics. These define um conversational triggers and branching logic. Basically, topics answer the question, what conversation paths does the agent handle? When someone says, I need help with my order, a topic recognizes that intent and starts the right conversation flow.

[01:15] Tools are the tool calls and the integrations. tools answer the questions, what can the agent actually do? An action might send an email or create a record in a database or call some external API. This is where the agent stops just talking and starts doing. Now, uh connectors, there are over a thousand pre-built connections to the enterprise systems. Uh Dynamics, SharePoint, Teams, Dataverse, you name it. Connectors. Connectors answer the question, how does the agent access data? They're the bridges to your actual real business systems and knowledge.

[02:02] These are grounding sources that keep the agent accurate and reduce hallucinate and reduce hallucinations. You can connect to SharePoint sites, websites, uploaded documents. The agent answers from your data, not just from what it learned during training. Here's how these components work together in a typical design flow. Step one, a topic detects the intent from the user input. Someone types something and the topic recognizes what they're asking for. Step two, an action calls a tool or an external service. The agent needs to do something. So, it triggers an action.

[02:47] Step three, a connector fetches or updates data. That action uses a connector to talk to an actual business system. Step four, a knowledge source provides context. Maybe the agent needs to look up a policy document or an FAQ or content to formulate a good response. Step five, the response is generated and sent back to the user.

[03:15] Let me give you a real example. A customer support agent with a topic called escalate issue. Uh when someone indicates that they need escalation, that topic triggers an action to create a case in Dynamics 365. The action uses the Dynamics connector to write that record and knowledge from SharePoint provides issue resolution history so that the agent can give context to whoever picks up the case.
